title: Creating Multilingual Mental Health Dialogue Datasets: Limits of Persona-Based Localization via Nationality and Language

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM performance disparities by comparing accuracy, error rates, and uncertainty (tie distance) when judging depression severity in synthetic clinical dialogues generated across four different languages (English, Mandarin, Bengali, and Hindi).

Modifying nationality parameters (e.g., United States, China, Bangladesh, India) in baseline clinical persona prompts to measure whether modifying geographic/national identity alters the downstream clinical consistency of generated symptoms.

Assessing how minimal parameter-based localization applied to English-centric personas fails to preserve culturally specific symptom expressions and structural interactions, leading to misclassification of depression severity in non-Western contexts.
